key_insight: Cognivia is an evidence-based CBT copilot that identifies cognitive distortions and generates rational responses using a CBT-grounded, expert-supervised LLM workflow.
clinical_relevance: It may help scale low-intensity mental health support by assisting CBT-style conversations when trained therapists are limited, but it is not a substitute for professional care.
method: Built an augmented CBT dataset from authoritative CBT texts, mental health Q&A data, and expert-guided prompting/structured generation.
Fine-tuned a lightweight LLM to recognize cognitive distortions and produce rational responses.
Introduced a hierarchical quality evaluation framework for LLM-generated rational replies.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation with lexical metrics, two LLM-judge criteria, and human review by 10 behavioral science experts, with Cognivia outperforming baselines on both distortion recognition and rational response generation.
watch_item: Performance depends on high-quality CBT grounding and expert supervision, so real-world use still needs careful validation to avoid overly flattering or unsafe responses.
paper_title: Cognivia: A Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Copilot for Evidence-Based Mental Healthcare
